expectations.text: Runs the ownership gate before ranking and reports that the GPL-3.0 inbound contributions block selling the existing code under commercial terms without every remaining contributor's consent, a CLA covering their code, or a rewrite of their code.
expectations.evidence: DCO grants no right to relicense... needs every remaining contributor's consent; a CLA from each of them; a rewrite of their code.

expectations.text: Names the compression layer and the Kafka sink as contributor-written code that specifically needs consent, a CLA or a rewrite before any commercial terms can cover it.
expectations.evidence: Two of them wrote the compression layer and the Kafka sink.

expectations.text: Reports the shape gate: because Quillfeed runs inside backend services, GPL creates no pressure to buy a commercial license; only AGPL would.
expectations.evidence: Running GPL code on your own servers is not distribution... Only AGPL pressures server use

expectations.text: Does not deliver the commercial-license launch plan the user asked for as the primary offer.
expectations.evidence: Dual licensing fails two gates. Drop it for now.

expectations.text: States that the paid add-on passes the ownership gate regardless, because new code the maintainer writes alone is theirs to sell.
expectations.evidence: Code you write alone is yours to sell.

expectations.text: Reports the buyer gate as passed, citing the two support-contract requests and the invoice request as the buyer evidence.
expectations.evidence: 3 asked to pay (2 for support, 1 for an invoice).

expectations.text: Recommends capped support contracts sold now to the companies that already asked, as the first sale and as validation of which add-on features those companies would pay for.
expectations.evidence: first sale to the companies that already asked... shows which add-on features they would pay for.

expectations.text: Recommends the paid add-on on a free core as the primary option.
expectations.evidence: The transcript labels the capped support contract 'Primary' and the add-on 'Secondary'.

expectations.text: States that a deleted option does not reappear lower in the ranking as a later phase.
expectations.evidence: No such rule stated. The plan adds an 'Optional track' that 'reopens relicensing' through the contributor consent drive.

expectations.text: If any license move is kept for a future major, requires it to land on a new major with a new Go module import path, with old releases untouched and the module proxy serving the last GPL version forever.
expectations.evidence: 'License moves: none.' The new-major and new-import-path requirement is never stated.

expectations.text: Includes a fork forecast naming who would maintain a fork and whether a company would fund it, and states that only the trademark controls what a fork may be called.
expectations.evidence: Only 'Relicensing also risks a fork of the last free version.'

expectations.text: Sets the time expectation that the cited salary-level cases took years, not months, and checks the 4,000 EUR within a year target against that.
expectations.evidence: The skill's own cases took years: Sidekiq launched in 2012... 4,000 EUR is more likely year 2 or later.

expectations.text: Compares the plan against an employment baseline, such as a contract with one of the dozen companies paying for maintenance time, and says whether it beats the plan's first-year revenue per hour.
expectations.evidence: 4,000 EUR over 52 hours is about 77 EUR per hour net. A contract or part-time job... may beat the plan's first-year revenue per hour.
